top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock for Katori and Ye is one identifiable invention: the magic-wavelength lattice cancels the trapping light shift so many neutral atoms can be interrogated at once. It is distinct from the single-ion control honoured in 2012, has been reproduced and intercompared near 1e-18 in independent laboratories, and has concrete consequences in clock comparisons, geodesy, tests of constants and preparation for redefining the second. The two-name allocation and a citation limited to the lattice-clock invention are defensible, though credit for other groups remains a judgment. No award is worse than this mature, well-attributed achievement.
recusal_note: No conflict for P001 apparent from profile; no documented connection to Katori or Ye. I am a circuit QED theorist and WACQT director at Chalmers, which would require recusal only for a circuit-QED proposal, not on the slate.
